title: Trump wants to meet Kim Jong Un again
ticker: Trump on meeting Kim Jong Un during Asia trip: "I may. That would be exciting"
North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles - fourth launch in about a month
Kim opens new defense museum featuring the Hwasong-20 ICBM
Trump to attend APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, in mid-November

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Welcome to KOWEN News.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: President Trump says he *may meet Kim Jong Un* on his trip to Asia next month.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: I get along with him, Trump said. *That would be exciting*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: But on the very same day, North Korea fired *multiple ballistic missiles*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: And a day later, Kim showed off a missile built to *reach the United States*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Here is what Trump said, how Pyongyang is answering, and whether a fourth Trump-Kim summit could really happen.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Reporters asked Trump on Monday whether he would meet Kim during his Asia trip.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: *I may*, Trump answered. *That would be exciting*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He added a line he has used many times before. *I get along with him*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Trump is expected to meet Chinese President *Xi Jinping* on the sidelines of the APEC summit in *Shenzhen*, China, in mid-November.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The Wall Street Journal has reported that Trump privately discussed meeting Kim *at that summit*. No meeting has been set.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In recent weeks, Trump has said he would like a meeting with Kim *this year*.

scenes.name: Donald Trump
scenes.quote: I may. That would be exciting. I get along with him.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Trump has long described his relationship with Kim as *warm*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: During his first term, the two leaders exchanged letters that Trump once called *love letters*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: At a 2018 rally, he even said of Kim, *we fell in love*. He wrote me beautiful letters.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Earlier this month, he also met Kim's old friend, a former basketball star. More on that in a moment.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Now he appears ready to try *one more time*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The two have met *three times*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In June 2018 in *Singapore*, the first-ever summit between a sitting U.S. president and a North Korean leader.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In February 2019 in *Hanoi*, where talks broke down over sanctions and nuclear sites, and ended *without a deal*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: And in June 2019 at the DMZ, where Trump became the first sitting U.S. president to *step into North Korea*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: None of those meetings produced a *diplomatic breakthrough*, and talks stopped altogether in 2019.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Trump's push has also brought back a familiar face. *Dennis Rodman*.

scenes.name: Dennis Rodman
scenes.quote: Trump: "The one who knew him best was Dennis Rodman."

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Earlier this month, the former NBA star appeared with Trump at a truck plant near *Dallas*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: No official reason was given for his visit.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Asked whether Rodman was helping broker peace, Trump talked about Kim instead. The one who knew him best, Trump said, *was Dennis Rodman*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Rodman struck up an unlikely friendship with Kim more than a decade ago, and traveled to North Korea *several times* between 2013 and 2017.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: So how did North Korea respond? Not with words. *With missiles*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The launch came just two days after North Korea marked the *81st anniversary* of its ruling Workers' Party.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: On Monday morning, the same day Trump spoke, North Korea fired *multiple ballistic missiles* toward the sea off its east coast.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: South Korea's military said one missile, launched from the Pyongyang area, flew *more than 900 kilometers*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Japan said at least two missiles were launched *17 minutes apart*, and one followed an *irregular* flight path. It suggested it may have been a *hypersonic weapon*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Pyongyang said it was testing an *upgraded component* for its tactical missiles.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: It was North Korea's *fourth* ballistic missile launch in about a month.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: On October third, Pyongyang also tested a *hypersonic intermediate-range missile*, designed to evade missile defenses in South Korea and Japan.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Japan's Defense Minister *Shinjiro Koizumi* condemned the latest test.

scenes.name: Kim Jong Un
scenes.quote: On display: the Hwasong-20, an ICBM capable of reaching the United States.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: A day later, state media released photos of Kim opening a new *Defense Revolution Museum*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He was joined by his wife *Ri Sol Ju* and his daughter, known as *Ju Ae*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The centerpiece was the *Hwasong-20*, an intercontinental ballistic missile capable of reaching *the U.S. mainland*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The Hwasong-20 has *not yet been flight-tested*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Another expert said turning temporary weapons shows into a permanent museum presents Kim's nuclear buildup as a *completed and enduring legacy*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: A display beside it appeared to show a *multiple-warhead* design, and a map with ranges stretching to the Middle East, Australia and South America.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: One South Korean analyst called it *propaganda* aimed at gaining an edge before a possible summit with Washington.

scenes.name: Kim Jong Un
scenes.quote: If the U.S. drops its absurd obsession with denuclearization, there is no reason not to sit down with them.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Kim has made his conditions clear.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Last year he said he still has *good memories* of Trump.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: But he said talks are only possible if Washington drops what he called its *absurd obsession with denuclearization*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Pyongyang still demands the U.S. end its *hostile policy* before any talks.

scenes.name: Kim Yo Jong
scenes.quote: The relationship between the two leaders remains excellent. However, the U.S.'s hostile policies haven't changed.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In August, when Trump first said he expected to meet Kim later this year, Kim's powerful sister answered.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The relationship between the two leaders *remains excellent*, she said. However, the U.S.'s *hostile policies* haven't changed.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: North Korea also denied there had been *any direct communication* with Washington.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: This month, she also called Seoul's demand for an apology over the mine blast *despicable*, and rejected an offer of *medical equipment* from the South.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: And South Korea finds itself in a *tricky spot*.

scenes.name: Lee Jae-myung
scenes.quote: Repeated missile launches violate U.N. Security Council resolutions. Stop immediately.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: President Lee Jae-myung's office said the launches *violate U.N. resolutions* and called for an immediate stop.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Just days earlier, Lee personally oversaw South Korea's first test of a *hypersonic missile*. Seoul's military called Monday's launch a *show of force* in response.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Lee's office said that weapon, once fully developed, would let Seoul *strike key targets by surprise*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Seoul had been working to help restart talks between Pyongyang and Washington, before a *landmine blast* in the DMZ wounded three South Korean soldiers.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: A joint South Korean and U.N. probe found the mines were *planted by North Korea*. Pyongyang denies it.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Lee pledged to *reopen dialogue* with the North in his very first speech after taking office in 2025.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Trump's outreach also comes as relations between Washington and Seoul are *strained*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In August, Trump ordered the Pentagon to *scale back military exercises* with South Korea.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He cited frustration that Seoul did not back U.S. operations against Iran, and said the drills sent an *inappropriate signal* to North Korea.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He has also threatened new trade penalties unless Seoul follows through on a *54 billion dollar* gas project in Alaska, part of a *350 billion dollar* investment pledge.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: So will Trump and Kim meet again?

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Prediction market *Polymarket* shows the odds rising, from about *19 percent* to *27 percent* in a single day.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Kim has so far *not answered* Trump's offers in public.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Even if a meeting happens, history shows that a handshake and a photo do not guarantee a *deal*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The main sticking point has not changed since 2019. Washington wants *denuclearization*. Pyongyang says that is *off the table*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Some reports name the *ASEAN summit in Manila* on November sixteenth as another possible venue.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: All eyes now turn to Trump's trip to *China in November*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Trump says he gets along with Kim. Kim, so far, is answering *with missiles*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: We'll keep following whether a *fourth summit* really happens.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: If you found this helpful, please *like and subscribe* for more.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: This has been KOWEN News. Thanks for watching.
